Voice: a tool turn that ends on filler is asked once more, never left silent
no ticket
ecf93dc7 · 6 files
After a tool result (often a refusal naming another tool), flash-lite sometimes ended the turn with only "Checking." / "Let me look." / "Checking the modules.": a filler, then silence. - FillerTurn: the rule, written down. After the LeadingFiller strip, filler only = an exact scripted filler, or one sentence of at most four words, no digit and no , ; : that starts with a filler opener (checking, looking, let me look, let me check, one moment, just a moment, on it, hold on) and whose next word, if any, is a plain continuer (the, now, into, that, ...). - GeminiTextLoop: after a tool ran, a round's text is held while it may still be filler and let go the moment it is not, so a filler line is never spoken. A filler-only end gets ONE more round, tool-free, with a system note (the lookup is finished; answer from the results or say plainly it could not be done). Filler again ends as NO_TEXT, the existing failure line; never a loop. - CascadeSession: counts only (reply_filler_continued, reply_filler_again); the failure line is said even after earlier words of the turn were heard. - Tests: the rule and its near misses, the streaming hold, at most one continuation, the empty last round after a leading filler, no change without a tool. Plus a check-in conversation carries no agenda block on any turn (pin + AgendaBlock.current over an empty read). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ClearPlanner offers a module only when its fault codes were READ (so a re-read can confirm) and it is positively known not to be a restraint module: an emissions address (7E0-7E7, ISO 15765-4) or a make-table name whose table is confirmed by its own restraint address answering in the same scan. Diagnostics step 3: pre-CAN path, and two parser fixes it found
no ticket
aa5753c2 · 4 files
Pre-CAN cars (J1850 VPW/PWM, ISO 9141-2, KWP on the K-line) get no module discovery and no header changes: generic Mode 03/07/0A only, with the slow-bus wait, and the scan says in words that the body, airbag, ABS and transmission computers of that era are not reachable with this dongle. Mode 0A is said to be a CAN-era feature, not "no codes". Fixes in the existing generic reader: - CAN Mode 03 answers start with a COUNT byte the legacy buses do not send. The old parser read it as half a code: "43 01 01 33" (P0133) came out as P0101. The connect now records the bus (ATDPN) and dtcCodes decodes by it; legacy replies read exactly as before. isValidDtcReply now sees an indexed CAN multi-frame ("0: 43 ..."). - "BUS INIT: ...OK" (a K-line init that worked) counted as a failure, so an XJ reply after a re-init read as dead. Only a bus-init line without OK counts now. ObdBluetoothManager.withDiagnosticLink holds the command mutex for a whole scan or clear (the poller waits), and its commands never count toward the PID-silence re-init. Diagnostics step 2: generic module scan on CAN
no ticket
60bbef39 · 16 files
Adapter identity (ATI, STI: ELM327 clone vs STN/OBDLink class), the bus from ATDPN, a key-off check (no engine answer = say so) and a moving check, then: generic engine codes (Mode 03/07/0A at the functional address, each answering ECU named), every candidate address probed with TesterPresent (quick list: 7E0-7E7, the make's named modules, common addresses; full sweep: 700-7F7, or 29-bit targets 00-FE), and each module that answers read with UDS 19 02 FF, falling back to KWP2000 18 / 13 only when UDS says it is the wrong service. Status bits in words (confirmed / pending / failing now / failed this cycle / history); test-not-complete alone is not a fault. Identity DIDs F190, F197, F187, F188, F18C, F111, F113 within the time budget. Refused, silent, cut-off and not-understood are recorded as such, never as "no codes". The receive filter and flow-control header are set explicitly per module and every AT reply is checked; a clone without manual flow control falls back and is noted. A response-pending reply gets one retry with the longest wait. The adapter state is put back in a NonCancellable finally. Read services only: no session, security, write, I/O control or routine service can be sent. Names come from tables that say their source (ISO 15765-4's 7E0-7E7, Ford community naming, the one public Mitsubishi address); restraint modules are flagged by table, by their own system name, or by a B00xx code. Not built and tested commit by commit: the branch tip is (see the report). - Notification buttons carry the held id (or the assumed car), so a tap after the dongle disconnects still answers; the assumed window keeps its dongle. - A connection that read no VIN retries once at engine start, and a reconnect inside the same drive that reads one carries the drive's data to the VIN's car (or to pending:vin:<VIN> when unknown). - No-VIN holds are keyed by dongle and session start, so two unanswered drives never pool. - State flips before a move, so no tick lands under the old id; session tallies clear on a new session, so a correction never moves an earlier drive's miles. - A VIN on the wrong car on file can be replaced (button, or the same answer 10 s to 5 min later); an immediate repeat does not count. - Voice switch answers only an open question (held or assumed) or reports a VIN-proved car; the car picker is a stored-data pick only; the Cars card covers corrections. - The spoken ask is marked asked only when the bus did not say "not now"; resolution-changed fires once per connect, when the car changed. OBD VIN attribution: one dongle, several cars, data never mixes

6aad691d · 25 files
On each connect, after ELM init and before anything records, the VIN is read once (bounded, one retry, never blocks the connect) and DongleCar.decide picks the car: - VIN on exactly one car on file: that car, even over a hand pick (said once). - VIN on no car (or on two): data held under pending:vin:<VIN>; a notification and a spoken Fleet raise ask which car (cars on file or a new car). - No VIN: the last car confirmed for this dongle is assumed and said in words, its window held back from upload until confirmed, corrected or the next connect; with no earlier answer, held under pending:obd:<mac> and asked. Samples, drives, trip summaries, code events and the capability scan are written under ActiveVehicle.recordingId; TelemetryRecorder waits for the decision and keeps a drive's car through a link-loss finalize. The answer (DongleCarController.answer) is one controller for voice (manage_vehicle switch via VehicleController.switchToOutcome, now with an honest success flag), the notification buttons and a Cars screen card. It writes the VIN to vehicle_specs (never silently over a different VIN), re-keys held data, or records a DriveReassignment rule for a corrected assumption, re-pushing drives and code events by sync_id. ObdSampleReconcile halts at held samples. registerDirect and VIN spec saves refuse while the car is unknown. No Room schema change, no server change, no new tool declaration. HeldTurnSink wraps the turn taker's Live sink: when armed, a tapped or woken conversation's first turn (manual activity only) is buffered, Vosk (already in the APK) reads it against the command vocabulary, and the matcher decides. A hit runs the same tool through LiveToolbox.dispatch, says the tool's own words with on-device speech and ends the conversation: Live ran no generation. A miss replays the held turn to Live start to end, so Kevin never repeats himself. Behind Settings key local_commands, OFF until it has run on the phone. Voice cost audit 2026-11-10 (ADR 0087). Kevin: "lets cut the toollist", "drop the spoken greeting and wake reply, can we seed a few scripted lines instead?", then "yes trim tools" (about 15 always-loaded core tools plus helpers). Tool diet (F1): service/tools/LiveSurface.kt folds the 93 top-level declarations into 24: 12 direct, 10 action tools whose action values are the old tool names, and two routers (ask: NON_BLOCKING domains; look_up: blocking). A call resolves to the old tool before anything name-keyed runs (session, controller, typed chat, dispatch), so confirm gates, read-through, write accounting and timeouts are unchanged; the response keeps the name the model called. Long caveats ride on results. Measured (chars/4): tools JSON 82,896 -> 29,723 chars, setup ~23,426 -> ~10,134 tokens. LiveSetupPayloadSizeTest asserts at most 24 declarations and 31,000 chars. Scripted line (F2): GREETING_PROMPT and WAKE_ACK_PROMPT are gone. A tap or wake word plays one of Kevin's 25 lines (assets/listen_cues/lines.json, earcon until clips exist) on Alfred's own track, on connect (CUE_TIMING), and the mic opens after it drains (Bluetooth settle included). Live context rides the system instruction. tools/render_listen_cues.py renders clips with a pluggable renderer. Usage (F7): a LIVE_AUDIT usage line per usageMetadata (counts by modality, thoughts); Live usage is max-folded within a generation and summed across them (it kept the MAX of the whole socket). Eval: tools/live_tool_eval/cases.jsonl (104 invented utterances, every old tool); LiveToolEvalCasesTest checks it offline, tools/live_tool_eval.py runs it on a key. 5e8c02db · 3 files
Crash records 2026-11-10: a SIGSEGV in wake-two-stage at a keyword hit (freed memory) and an uncaught IllegalStateException from startRecording on an uninitialized AudioRecord. Both were beginListening and releaseSpeechService racing on different threads: a release mid-open closed the new Vosk recognizer, or released the new record between its state check and startRecording. WakeCaptureGate serialises open and teardown, runs each chunk's native work only while its capture is open, and a teardown takes the objects out of the fields before freeing them. A capture that will not open gives the mic back and the watchdog backs off instead of throwing.
